title: Exercise item
description: An exercise cannot be issued without a grading spec. Three tiers exist per lesson: anchored (taken from an external source with a real answer), variant (changed conditions, still mechanically checkable), modeling (open, rubric-judged).

tier.description: anchored: a real problem lifted from an external source, so its difficulty is not self-assessed. variant: parameters or conditions changed, still mechanically checkable. modeling: a real situation the learner must set up themselves, judged by rubric. Required for everything except an explain-back, which is not drawn from a source, not a variant of one, and not an open-ended task, so no tier describes it.

anchor_kind.description: REQUIRED for the anchored tier. What kind of external source fixes this item's difficulty. A course with no textbook still anchors: a derivation in the original paper, the semantics in official documentation, a public course assignment, or a published benchmark number. What is never allowed is an anchored-tier item the system invented and then called hard.

source_ref.description: REQUIRED for the anchored tier. Precise enough to find again, e.g. Strang 6.1 problem 14 p.288, or Vaswani 2017 eq.(1) sec.3.2.1, or CS231n assignment 2 Q4.

assets.description: Scaffold files handed to the learner (starter code, input decks, data).

grader.description: HARD GATE. No grading spec means the item may not be issued.

checker_id.description: REQUIRED when type is checker. Names a checker the course adapter registered. The core runs it and reads its verdict; it does not know what the checker inspects, which is what keeps any one discipline out of this file.

spec.description: Grader-specific payload: expected value and tolerance, test file path, log keys to parse, observable ranges, rubric id.

rubric_id.description: Required when grader.type is rubric. Modeling-tier items always need one.

answer_key.description: Kept out of anything sent to the learner. Sent to the grader agent.

capability_required.description: capability_id values this item needs in order to run for real.

degraded_form.description: What this item becomes when the capability is missing. Chosen from capabilities.json, never improvised mid-lesson.

depth.description: The depth this item probes. An item deeper than the concept depth_target may not be issued on the main line; that is what a sidequest or an explicit raise is for.

interleaved.description: Part of a mixed drill. The prompt must not say which concept or method it belongs to - that choice is the thing being practised, and revealing it turns the item back into blocked practice.

transfer_dimensions.description: REQUIRED when this item is used as a transfer test. Naming the dimension is what makes the claim checkable. The criterion this replaces - an open-ended item, or one spanning two concepts - moves only along knowledge_domain, which is why an item that names only that dimension is treated as the weak case and warned about.

mixed_from.description: lesson_id values this item was drawn across when it belongs to a mixed set. Recorded so that a drill claiming to mix can be checked: drawing several items from one lesson is not mixing, because the lesson itself tells the learner which method applies.

reveals_method.description: True when the wording tells the learner which method or concept to use. Harmless in a single-topic set and fatal in a mixed one: choosing the method is the thing a mixed set practises, so revealing it turns the item back into single-topic practice while still looking mixed.

response.description: How the learner supplies the answer. Separate from `form`, which is what their mind is doing, because the same cognitive work can be answered by typing a derivation, by choosing between three candidate derivations, or by filling the two steps that carry the point - identical evidence, very different amounts of typing. This block is required, and it is required for one specific reason: when it did not exist, the shape of the answer was decided in the moment by whoever was teaching. That produced a good interactive form for twenty minutes and then quietly reverted to a wall of prose, because nothing on disk remembered the decision and nothing could refuse an item that ignored it.

fields.description: The named slots the answer is made of, for fill_blanks and for a multi-part numeric or free_text item. Naming them is what lets the answer be stored as data rather than as a paragraph somebody has to read back later, and it is why a learner can answer part 3 without retyping parts 1 and 2.

expects_notation.description: True when answering this slot means writing something ordinary prose typing handles badly.

options.description: For mode choice. At least two, and the wrong ones have to be things someone could actually believe: options nobody would pick turn a choice item into a free pass while looking like an assessment.

why_wrong.description: For a distractor: the mistaken belief that leads here. Written when the item is written, so that choosing it can be answered with the misconception rather than with a repetition of the right answer.

expects_notation.description: True when answering this item at all requires notation - a formula, a structure, a diagram, a table, non-Latin script. Checked against how this learner said they can supply notation.

why.description: Why this mode for this item. One line.
